title: The Employee That Worked on the Longest Task
summary: Given n employees with unique ids from 0 to n-1, and a 2D integer array logs detailing each employee's task completion times, return the id of the employee who worked the longest on a single task.
statement: Given n employees with unique ids from 0 to n-1, and a 2D integer array logs detailing each employee's task completion times, return the id of the employee who worked the longest on a single task. If multiple employees worked the same longest time, return the one with the smallest id.
constraints: Tasks occur consecutively in log order; each log is [employee_id,end_time].
A task duration is its end time minus the preceding task end, or minus zero for the first task.
Return the employee with the longest single task, breaking ties by smaller id.
hints: Keep the previous task’s ending time.
For each log compute duration=end-previous, then advance previous.
Replace the answer for a longer duration or an equal duration with smaller employee id.
Each duration is computed once from consecutive endpoints and the comparison implements the exact maximum and tie rules.
editorial: Each duration is computed once from consecutive endpoints and the comparison implements the exact maximum and tie rules.

tests.explanation: Durations are three, two, four, and six; employee one owns the longest task.
The last three durations are six, five, and five, so employee three wins.
